tasks.short: Demonstrate and sell hair care products and cosmetics

steps.what: Discuss the patron's needs and demonstrate hair care products and cosmetics
Answer questions and agree the products the patron wants to buy

tasks.design: Retain the personal demonstration and sales conversation. Existing product instructions may remain in {DOCS}, but no automated recommendation or persuasion step is added.
tasks.previous_blocker: The value is showing how a product feels and works for this patron.
tasks.enabler_now: No new technology is required for the proposed unchanged workflow.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing commercial incentives with the patron's preferences and suitability.
tasks.human_edge: Demonstrate the technique and respond to hesitation without pressure.
tasks.altitude: Demonstration and sales time and rights stay the same.

reach.task: Coach staff on explaining product use honestly
reach.learn: Product instructions and responsible sales conversations

evidence.claim: Demonstration and personalised product discussion remain physical and relational work in this design.

assumptions: Boundary ends with the agreed selection; payment and checkout records are separate and must not be counted twice.
Patron preferences are heard directly in s1 with all time retained. No structured profile or machine recommendation is assumed.
Check existing product information before adding software; no build is proposed.
Zero incremental upkeep because no new content service, data feed or automation is introduced.
research_questions: Which patron questions require seeing or trying the product in person?

already_counted.description: Demonstrate products and discuss the purchase

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100; gross and net zero. Retain the demonstration and discussion rather than assume the sales conversation can be shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Order, display and maintain salon supplies

steps.what: Check supplies, count usable stock and identify replenishment needs
Select quantities, check prices and order supplies
Receive, display and maintain supplies, checking condition and storage

tasks.design: Use saved order lines in {PROCUREMENT} or {PARTNER_PORTAL} to reuse supplier codes and pack sizes. The hairstylist still counts stock, chooses quantities and confirms the final order, then handles every delivery and display physically.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated catalogue entry adds effort even when the same supplies are reordered.
tasks.enabler_now: Native saved baskets can reuse stable lines without an automatic demand forecast.
tasks.still_hard: Unrecorded salon consumption, substitutions and product condition.
tasks.human_edge: Spot unsuitable stock and decide whether a substitute is appropriate.
tasks.altitude: Less re-entry on orders; stock care and purchasing limits remain unchanged.

reach.task: Resolve a supplier pack-size or delivery discrepancy
reach.learn: Order units, catalogue codes and local approval limits

evidence.claim: Saved supplier order lines can reduce repeated entry while people choose quantities and check the order.

assumptions: Boundary covers stylist stock checks, orders and physical maintenance. Supplier fulfilment and finance payment remain outside and unchanged.
Hairstylist produces item id, usable count and requested quantity during s1 with all 25 hours retained. No par-level feed or consumption forecast is assumed.
Supplier maintains catalogue item, pack unit and price in the existing portal; the stylist checks those fields during s2's retained 12.5 hours. New saved-line upkeep is charged below.
Missing codes or unsuitable saved lines use manual ordering. Test native baskets before custom code and never order on a stale default quantity.
s2 confirmation binds the finished basket and destination within existing purchasing authority; changed lines require confirmation again. Physical receipt and displays retain all 50 hours.
unknowns: Who may place salon supply orders
research_questions: How much order time is repeated entry rather than quantity choice or supplier exceptions?

already_counted.description: Count supplies, review and confirm orders, receive and display products

incremental.description: Refresh saved lines and check changed pack sizes or discontinued items

approvals.approved_version: Final supplier basket including item, quantity, pack size, total and delivery destination; edits void confirmation

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=25+12.5+50=87.5; gross 12.5 minus upkeep 1 gives net 11.5. E1 scenario halves ordering effort on repeated lines only; frequent substitutions or one-off supplies may leave no net gain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Operate cash registers and receive patron payments

steps.what: Confirm services and products and enter the cash register bill
Receive payments from patrons, operate the terminal or handle cash and change
Record payment status and issue receipts for completed payments

tasks.design: Configure service-price lookup and terminal-linked receipts in the salon checkout category of {OTHER}. The hairstylist confirms what was actually delivered, approves the final charge and retains cash handling, customer interaction and payment exceptions.
tasks.previous_blocker: Services and prices can be re-entered at checkout and payment status copied separately.
tasks.enabler_now: A salon checkout can reuse service lines and a terminal outcome.
tasks.still_hard: Changed services, split payments, declined cards and disputed totals.
tasks.human_edge: Resolve a billing query respectfully and handle money accurately.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated checkout entry; payment handling and refund authority do not expand.

evidence.claim: Salonized supports salon payments and financial overviews, and Treatwell Connect supports contactless payments; this establishes checkout capability rather than a measured saving.
Reusing price lines and terminal outcomes can reduce duplicate register entry; cash and payment exceptions still take human time.

assumptions: Boundary is stylist checkout, not treatment delivery, customer payment time or end-of-day bookkeeping. Patron time is not claimed as a labour saving.

In s1 the hairstylist produces actual service codes, product codes, quantities and any permitted discount, retaining 24 hours for capture and checking. Salon manager already maintains service codes and prices outside checkout; additional mapping checks are charged below. Appointment bookings are not assumed to prove services delivered.

In s2 the terminal produces transaction id, amount, currency and success or failure; hairstylist produces the confirmed cash amount for cash payments. All 45 hours of payment interaction remain. s3 retains 6 hours for receipt choice, cash status entry and failed or unmatched payments.
Missing price or terminal linkage uses manual checkout and receipt issue. Test native checkout and terminal options before integration; existing processing runtime earns no labour saving.
Approval in s2 binds the final bill before payment initiation; a changed charge requires a fresh confirmation. No automatic refunds are included.
research_questions: Does native checkout linkage reduce re-entry without increasing unmatched payments or incorrect service charges?

already_counted.description: Capture delivered services, confirm the charge, handle payments and resolve receipts

incremental.description: Check changed service-price mappings and terminal receipt errors

approvals.approved_version: Final bill revision with service and product lines, adjustments and total before payment; edits void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=24+45+6=75; gross 25 less upkeep 1 gives net 24. E1 scenario reduces bill entry by 40% and receipt work by 60%, leaving all payment handling. Existing linked tills or many cash exceptions can leave no additional saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Provide permitted scalp treatment and advise medical referral

steps.what: Discuss scalp concerns and advise medical treatment for chronic or contagious conditions
Administer only authorised therapeutic scalp medication when the service is permitted

tasks.design: Retain the conversation, referral advice and any locally authorised physical treatment with the practitioner. No automated diagnosis, medication selection or additional health-data record in {CRM} is proposed.
tasks.previous_blocker: A task title does not establish that a salon practitioner is authorised to provide a particular medical treatment.
tasks.enabler_now: No new technology or broader clinical authority is assumed.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising limits, deferring unsuitable services and communicating sensitively.
tasks.human_edge: Notice concerns and help the patron seek an appropriate professional assessment.
tasks.altitude: No change to permitted scope, clinical authority or time spent with patrons.

reach.task: Clarify which scalp services staff may provide locally
reach.learn: Scope of practice, product instructions and referral procedures

evidence.claim: The design retains human referral and permitted treatment rather than inferring medical authority from an occupational task statement.

assumptions: Boundary covers the stylist's discussion and only treatment already permitted by local rules, training and product conditions. Diagnosis, prescribing and medical treatment by a clinician are outside it.
The hairstylist gathers the patron's account and observes in s1 with all 60 hours retained. No structured condition label, automated triage or free health-data capture is assumed.
If the service is outside local scope it is deferred; the graph is not permission to administer medication.
Native software is unnecessary here. Zero incremental upkeep because no automated advice, new record or data feed is introduced.
research_questions: Which listed services are actually within practitioners' local scope and which are deferred?

already_counted.description: Discuss concerns, advise referral and deliver or defer permitted treatment

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100, R=100 and net zero. All practitioner conversation, judgement and physical care remain; no saving is claimed from referring a patron to another professional.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The hairstylist keeps personal advice and hands-on services while spending less time on repeated supply and checkout entry.
reach: Help the salon supervisor investigate payment mismatches
Work with purchasing on changed pack sizes
role.ambitious_version: A practitioner who can focus on patrons while keeping stock orders and bills accurate without duplicate entry.
